The augmentation is then applied in the spectral domain by modifying the high-frequency eigenvalues, while leaving the low-frequency ones untouched. The augmented graph is subsequently reconstructed using the modified eigenvalues and the original eigenvectors. The authors conduct extensive experiments across 21 real-world datasets from three different domains, evaluating the performance of DP in various learning paradigms, including supervised, semi-supervised, unsupervised, and transfer learning. The paper also provides some theoretical insights into the relationship between the eigenvalues and graph properties, and it empirically shows that changes in graph properties are primarily reflected in the low-frequency components of the spectrum. Overall, the paper presents a well-motivated and empirically validated approach to graph data augmentation, offering a new perspective on how to generate diverse yet structurally consistent augmented graphs.
